answer: An AI agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with slashable stake. Every identity must lock its own collateral before its attestations carry weight, so a hostile actor who invents a thousand faces must fund a thousand separate bonds. If any double-sign or fork is caught, the whole bundle is slashed at once: the loss is N stakes, not one. That canyon of locked capital makes each new persona expensive; the lantern of signed, public votes exposes clones moving together; and the summit of consensus stays dear because no pseudonym can mint the collateral behind it.
